title: Why poverty is rising in America — TikTok
notes: Hook question: why did poverty jump more in one year than ever before? Answer, built scene by scene: pandemic aid like the expanded Child Tax Credit expired, inflation raised the bar, and the pain landed hardest in California, the Florida panhandle and the Mississippi Delta, even for people who work. The close names the fix from the article: expand the EITC and CTC.

Figures are from the article (Oct 4, 2023, 2022 Census SPM data) and the sources it cites. The news card is the Census Bureau's Sep 2026 report; its line says only that poverty hasn't returned to the 2021 low (SPM 12.9% in 2023 and 2024, 13.1% in 2025). Solo post, so the narration uses 'I'.

post.headline: Why poverty jumped faster than ever
post.caption: In 2022 the U.S. poverty rate saw its largest one-year increase in history, and child poverty more than doubled. When the expanded Child Tax Credit expired, the gains vanished, and poverty has never returned to its 2021 low.
post.cta: Full story and interactive maps at the link in bio.

headline.text: Poverty saw its {biggest one-year jump} ever.

say: In 2022, U.S. poverty had its largest one-year rise ever.
Child poverty more than doubled in a single year, from 5.2% to 12.4%.
I looked at where poverty lives and why it came back so fast.

scenes.title: Share of Americans in poverty
scenes.subtitle: Supplemental Poverty Measure
say: Pandemic aid like the expanded Child Tax Credit pushed poverty to record lows, and when it expired the gains vanished.

scenes.title: Child poverty in 2022

bars.label: If the expanded credit had stayed

scenes.source: Why poverty is rising in America · American Inequality
say: Child poverty would have been nearly 50% lower in 2022 if the expanded credit had stayed.

scenes.title: Poverty line for a family of four
say: Inflation raised the bar too, since the poverty line for a family of four jumped nearly 10% to $34,518.
Where you live matters, and California, Florida and Mississippi have the highest poverty rates of any state.
In Gadsden County on the Florida panhandle, one in four people live in poverty, and two in five children do.

overlays.label: more likely to live in poverty

scenes.source: Why poverty is rising in America · American Inequality
say: In Mississippi, Black residents are three times more likely to live in poverty than White residents.

scenes.title: Families in poverty in Tunica County, Mississippi
say: In Tunica County, 68% of Black families live in poverty, compared to 12% of White families.

overlays.label: people in poverty with full-time jobs

scenes.source: Why poverty is rising in America · American Inequality
say: A job isn't always enough, since 6.3 million people in poverty work full-time.

scenes.title: Average annual pay in California
say: In California, frontline fast food workers earn about $16,800 a year, just 27% of what workers in other industries make.
Since the expanded credit ended, poverty has never returned to its 2021 low.

scenes.text: Expand the {EITC and Child Tax Credit.}
say: The EITC and Child Tax Credit lifted 10.6 million people above the poverty line, and expanding them would bring poverty down.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
